data.raw_text:
web3 gaming has a focus problem.
everyone keeps building for the same western pc crowd… same discord servers, same wallet first onboarding that scares normal people away.

meanwhile 3.5 billion mobile gamers are already outside playing.
that’s the part most people ignore.
@elympics_ai didn’t.

instead of building another token farm, they built infrastructure. the boring part. the hard part. the part that actually decides if a competitive game survives.

server authority so you can’t manipulate matches from the client side.
ai anti cheat watching patterns in real time.
proof of game verification so outcomes match actual gameplay.
replays anyone can audit.

and they didn’t lock it to one chain. ton, abstract, base. multichain from day one.
but the real difference is the model.

play2earn prints tokens until everyone dumps.
play2win runs zero sum tournaments. entry fees fund prizes. winners take from losers. no inflation spiral. just competition.

your wins stay recorded on chain. no database disappearing when a project shuts down. your skill becomes identity.

look at what’s live already.

@PenguClash just wrapped season 26. four themes in four weeks. weekly resets, weekend tournaments, real rewards. 13k+ soulbound tokens minted for players who showed up early.

plooshy pile up quietly pulling 20k+ unique players and 1.5k daily actives. 250 new players joining every single day. that’s not bot traffic. that’s retention.

smash and crash on abstract. pure skill physics. no rng excuses.

fast matches. mobile friendly. telegram access. web access.

and here’s the bigger angle.

mobile gaming did 92b last year.
india is 90 percent mobile only.
southeast asia runs on phones.
latin america lives on messaging apps.

people in manila are not buying gaming pcs.
people in lagos are not downloading wallets before trying a game.

they open an app. they play. they compete with friends.

elympics built for that reality.

local payments. mobile first design. social tournament culture. on chain records without forcing people to “learn crypto” first.
that’s the part most web3 projects still don’t get.

early stage? yes.
volatile? obviously.
but the infrastructure is live. the games are shipping weekly. the players are showing up.

web3 can keep building for 100 million western gamers.
or it can build for the 3.5 billion already playing. just a personal opinion 👀
